title: Will Amazon launch any Amazon Leo (Project Kuiper) satellites between July 26 and August 8, 2026?
description:
Amazon Leo (formerly Project Kuiper) is Amazon's planned low-Earth-orbit broadband constellation of 3,236 satellites. As of late July 2026, roughly 396 operational satellites are in orbit across 15 flights, using ULA Atlas V 551, Arianespace Ariane 64, and SpaceX Falcon 9 vehicles. The most recent launch was LA-08 (Atlas V 551, 29 satellites) on July 2, 2026 — which Amazon has stated was the final mission in its "Leo Atlas" campaign. Amazon says its next ULA launch ("Leo Vulcan 1", ~45 satellites on Vulcan Centaur) is planned but has no firm public date; some sources list it around September 2026. Additional Falcon 9 missions (about 10 remaining of a 13+ contract) and New Glenn missions are contracted but not publicly dated. Historically the cadence has been roughly monthly, and Amazon faces FCC deployment milestones for its constellation. As of late July 2026, no Amazon Leo launch was publicly pinned to the July 26–August 8, 2026 window.

It resolves based on the "List of Amazon Leo launches" Wikipedia page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Amazon_Leo_launches): if that page's launch history table shows an entry with a liftoff date within the window, the question resolves YES; otherwise NO. A launch counts on the date liftoff occurs regardless of whether the payload reaches orbit successfully. If the Wikipedia page is unavailable, resolution follows Amazon Leo's official mission updates or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).

A launch that is scrubbed, aborted before liftoff, or delayed past August 8, 2026 does not count. Only the actual liftoff time matters, not any prior planned date.

title: Will the UK add a new Cyber-regime sanctions designation between July 25 and August 8, 2026?
description:
The UK operates a dedicated cyber sanctions regime under the Cyber (Sanctions) (EU Exit) Regulations 2020, targeting persons involved in "relevant cyber activity". All current designations are held on the UK Sanctions List, maintained by the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO); the older OFSI Consolidated List was closed on 28 January 2026 and is no longer updated. The UK Sanctions List page publishes an update history logging each change, including the number of new designations and the regime affected, and was last updated on 24 July 2026. Cyber-regime designations have historically arrived in periodic batches (roughly a handful per year) rather than continuously.

On 13 July 2026, the UK and EU announced their first joint cyber-sanctions package targeting Russian cyber networks, publicly attributing operations (including a thwarted attack on Poland's energy grid) to the FSB's 16th Centre (Centre 16). The UK added 24 individuals and entities aligned with the EU measures. The EU adopted its largest-ever cyber-sanctions package the same day (9 individuals, 4 entities), and separately adopted its 21st Russia sanctions package on 23 July 2026 (published in the Official Journal 24 July 2026), which included roughly 250 listings. Officials have signalled continued expansion of cyber-related designations, though a large cyber batch having just landed on 13 July may reduce the likelihood of another cyber-specific addition in the immediately following weeks.

title: Will a new bluetongue focus be officially confirmed in Pontevedra or Ourense before August 8, 2026?
description:
Bluetongue (Spanish: "lengua azul") is a viral disease of ruminants transmitted by Culicoides midges; it does not affect humans. In Spain it is monitored under the national bluetongue and EHD surveillance programme, with foci notified through the Red de Alerta Sanitaria Veterinaria and confirmed by the Laboratorio Central de Veterinaria (LCV) in Algete. For the 2026-2027 vector season (which began 1 April 2026), Spain notifies immediately the first focus of each serotype in each province.

Galicia has four provinces: A Coruña, Lugo, Pontevedra and Ourense. In 2025 (the 2025-2026 season), serotypes 3 (BTV-3) and 8 (BTV-8) circulated across all four Galician provinces. For 2026, the first foci were confirmed on 6 July 2026 in A Coruña (BTV-3 in Brión/A Baña and BTV-8 in Narón). On 23 July 2026 the Xunta reported the season's third Galician focus: BTV-8 in a cattle holding in Meira (Lugo). As of 23 July 2026, no 2026-2027 focus had yet been confirmed in Pontevedra or Ourense.

Both Pontevedra and Ourense are within the peninsular restricted zone and had detections in prior seasons (serotype 4 in sentinel holdings in 2022-2023; serotypes 3 and 8 present across Galicia in 2025-2026). July and August fall within the period of maximum Culicoides vector activity, so the risk of onward spread to these provinces during the window is meaningful but not certain. New foci and serotype maps are published in MAPA's recurring bluetongue epidemiological situation updates and in Xunta Consellería do Medio Rural press notes.

Official confirmation means the focus is recorded in a Ministry of Agriculture (MAPA) bluetongue epidemiological situation update (published at https://www.mapa.gob.es/es/ganaderia/temas/sanidad-animal-higiene-ganadera/sanidad-animal/enfermedades/lengua-azul/), announced by the Xunta de Galicia Consellería do Medio Rural, or reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). If no such focus in Pontevedra or Ourense has a confirmation/notification date within that window, the question resolves NO. As of July 23, 2026, the only 2026-2027 season foci confirmed in Galicia are in A Coruña (serotypes 3 and 8) and Lugo (serotype 8); Pontevedra and Ourense have none.

A "focus" is a laboratory-confirmed detection of bluetongue virus in a livestock holding (confirmed by the Laboratorio Central de Veterinaria de Algete or a regional veterinary laboratory). "New" means a focus whose confirmation/notification date falls within the July 25 to August 7, 2026 window; a holding already counted as a focus before July 25, 2026 does not count. The binding trigger is the confirmation/notification date attributed to the focus, not the date the bulletin or press note is published: a focus dated within the window still resolves YES even if the source publishing it appears after August 8, 2026, so resolution waits for publication rather than resolving NO prematurely. Where a source reports foci only at province and serotype level (e.g., MAPA's national map showing the first focus of each serotype per province), a province-level entry for Pontevedra or Ourense dated within the window is sufficient.

title: Will the H3 rocket carrying QZS-7 (Michibiki 7) reach orbit by August 8, 2026?
description:
Japan's Quasi-Zenith Satellite System (QZSS), known as MICHIBIKI, is a regional satellite navigation system that augments GPS over the Asia-Oceania region. QZS-7 (MICHIBIKI No. 7) is a satellite intended to help build out the constellation toward a seven-satellite configuration that would let Japan provide positioning independent of GPS.

The satellite is scheduled to launch aboard H3 Launch Vehicle Flight No. 9 (H3 F9), the flagship rocket jointly developed by JAXA and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries. As of JAXA's most recent press releases (dated June 15, 2026, and updated July 8, 2026), the primary launch date is August 7, 2026 (JST), with a launch window of 04:30–06:00 JST (19:30–21:00 UTC on August 6, 2026), from the Yoshinobu Launch Complex at Tanegashima Space Center. JAXA has reserved backup launch periods of August 8–31, 2026 and September 3–30, 2026, with launch times set individually per day.

This launch is a return-to-flight for the H3 program. On December 22, 2025, H3 Flight No. 8 carrying QZS-5 (MICHIBIKI No. 5) failed: JAXA's investigation traced the loss to manufacturing-induced delamination in the Payload Support Structure (a CFRP–aluminum honeycomb satellite adapter), which buckled during fairing separation, damaged the second stage's hydrogen tank piping, and caused the upper-stage engine to shut down early, stranding the satellite in an unusable orbit. JAXA suspended subsequent H3 launches, including F9, and formally postponed QZS-7 in February 2026 pending the investigation. Corrective measures include a redesigned bolted-joint payload adapter and enhanced fairing inspections. The H3's earlier record is mixed: the maiden flight (F1) failed in March 2023, but Flights F2 through F7 succeeded before the F8 failure. Both schedule slips (weather at Tanegashima, technical holds) and elevated failure risk following F8 are relevant to this launch.

title: Will SpaceX conduct a static fire test of a Starship Flight 14 vehicle on or before August 8, 2026?
description:
SpaceX's Starship is a fully reusable super-heavy launch system (Super Heavy booster + Starship upper stage) flown from Starbase, Texas. Before each integrated flight, SpaceX typically conducts static fire tests — holding the vehicle down and igniting its Raptor engines — of the booster and/or ship as a key preflight milestone.

As of July 25, 2026, SpaceX has flown 13 integrated flight tests. Flight 12 (the Block 3 / V3 debut) flew May 22, 2026. Flight 13 launched July 24, 2026, on a suborbital trajectory with nominal ship splashdown and a hard booster splashdown; no tower catch was attempted. Ahead of Flight 13, the ship (Ship 40) completed a full-duration six-engine static fire on July 2, 2026, and the booster had also been static fired before rollout.

Flight 14 is described as "Starship Orbital Flight 1," the program's first orbital-injection attempt. As of July 25, 2026, no hardware testing campaign for Flight 14 has been publicly documented. SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell's roadmap reportedly targeted a roughly monthly cadence with Flight 14 in August, but trackers list only "Q3 2026 (TBD)," and the Flight 12→13 turnaround was about two months. Whether SpaceX begins Flight 14 static fire testing within roughly two weeks of Flight 13 is therefore genuinely uncertain. Starbase testing is closely tracked and promptly reported by SpaceX and spaceflight media.

title: Will a Senate cloture motion related to the CLARITY Act (H.R. 3633) be filed before August 8, 2026?
description:
The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act ("CLARITY Act", H.R. 3633) is a crypto market-structure bill that passed the U.S. House on July 17, 2025, by 294–134. The Senate Banking Committee advanced an amended version 15–9 on May 14, 2026, and the bill was placed on the Senate Legislative Calendar as Calendar No. 423 on June 1, 2026, making it eligible for floor consideration.

Under Senate Rule XXII, ending debate on major legislation requires invoking cloture with 60 votes. In practice, only the Majority Leader (John Thune) realistically brings such a bill to the floor and files the cloture motion; a cloture vote cannot occur until the second day of session after filing. With a 53–47 Republican majority and likely GOP defections (Hawley and Paul reported as probable no votes), supporters need roughly 5–7 Democratic crossover votes for cloture, and negotiations over ethics provisions and specific policy language have been ongoing.

As of mid-to-late July 2026, no cloture motion had been filed on H.R. 3633 and no floor vote had been scheduled. Advocates targeted floor consideration as early as the week of July 20, 2026, but competing priorities (NDAA, appropriations, nominations) have crowded the calendar. The Senate works only through roughly August 7 before an August 10–September 11 recess, making the pre-recess window the practical last chance for 2026 action. Cloture filings are recorded in the Congressional Record, on Congress.gov's "All Actions" for the bill, and on the Senate's official cloture motions list.

A unanimous-consent agreement to proceed without any cloture motion being filed does not count. Cloture motions filed before July 25, 2026 do not count.

title: Will the Argentine Senate give final approval to the 'Ley Hojarasca' before August 8, 2026?
description:
The "Ley Hojarasca" (formally a bill to derogate obsolete legislation, promoted by Federico Sturzenegger's deregulation ministry) seeks to repeal roughly 60 laws and decrees the government considers obsolete or contrary to individual liberties. The Chamber of Deputies granted media sanción on May 20, 2026 (approximately 138 in favor, 96 against, 9 abstentions), sending it to the Senate as expediente C.D.-1/26.

In the Senate, a joint plenary of the Constitutional Affairs and General Legislation committees issued a favorable majority dictamen (signed without modifications to the Deputies' text), leaving the bill ready for a floor vote. Because the Senate's majority dictamen keeps the Deputies' text unchanged, a favorable floor vote would grant definitive sanción, turning the bill into law.

Block leaders agreed to include the Ley Hojarasca on the agenda of a session scheduled for August 6, 2026, the first session after the winter recess. That agenda is crowded: it also includes the resumption of the debate on the "Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada" bill (whose July 16 session went into recess until August 6), a new Mental Health law, and a "false accusations" bill. Senate allies have at times imposed a rule of prioritizing one main topic per session, and treatment of Hojarasca could be delayed if the property-rights debate consumes the session or if the item is not reached. Reports have varied on the exact schedule, making it genuinely uncertain whether a final vote occurs within the resolution window.

title: Will Marquita Bradshaw win the 2026 Tennessee Democratic U.S. Senate primary?
description:
Tennessee holds its statewide primary elections on August 6, 2026. In the Democratic primary for the U.S. Senate seat currently held by Republican Bill Hagerty (who is unopposed in his primary), five candidates are certified: Marquita Bradshaw, Maria Brewer, Kevin Lee McCants, Civil Miller-Watkins, and Diana Onyejiaka.

Marquita Bradshaw is an environmental justice activist and staffing consultant who won the 2020 Tennessee Democratic Senate primary in a widely unexpected upset with about 35.5% of the vote, becoming the Democratic nominee (she lost the general election). In the 2024 primary she ran again but lost decisively to state Representative Gloria Johnson, taking about 21.8% to Johnson's 70.2%. In 2026 she faces a field of comparatively lesser-known challengers, and no prominent elected official is in the race.

There has been no public polling of this primary. The general expectation, reflected in thin prediction-market pricing, favors Bradshaw given her name recognition and prior nomination, but a multi-candidate field with low-turnout, low-information primary voters introduces meaningful uncertainty. Official and unofficial results will be published by the Tennessee Secretary of State's Division of Elections and reported by major news organizations on election night, August 6, 2026.

title: Will a Russian gasoline export ban be in force during August 1–8, 2026?
description:
Russia has repeatedly imposed temporary bans on fuel exports since 2023 to stabilize its domestic market, especially amid the 2025–2026 fuel crisis worsened by Ukrainian drone strikes on refineries. Government Resolution No. 78 of January 31, 2026 extended a ban on gasoline and diesel exports until July 31, 2026, but initially exempted direct producers for gasoline. On April 2, 2026, Resolution No. 362 expanded the gasoline export ban to also cover producers through July 31, 2026, with narrow exemptions for intergovernmental supply agreements (e.g., Mongolia). A separate July 2, 2026 decree by PM Mishustin allowed some refineries to produce lower-quality Euro-3 gasoline for domestic use only (non-exportable) through end-2026, but this is a quality derogation, not a general export ban. As of late July 2026, Interfax had reported that a renewed producer gasoline ban was 'almost decided' and would likely cover a full quarter, and Deputy PM Novak has said Russia may reimpose bans 'if necessary.' However, no government resolution extending or reimposing a gasoline export ban beyond July 31, 2026 had been published as of late July 2026.

Resolution relies on the Russian Government's official decisions page (http://government.ru/en/docs/) or reporting from [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) confirming that such a resolution is in effect during that window. Bans covering only diesel, jet fuel, or other fuels but not motor gasoline do not count.

title: Will the U.S. President formally transmit the U.S.–Saudi Arabia civilian nuclear cooperation ("123") agreement to Congress before August 7, 2026?
description:
On July 22, 2026, the United States and Saudi Arabia signed a civil nuclear cooperation agreement (a "Section 123 agreement" under the U.S. Atomic Energy Act), signed by U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright and Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman, alongside a bilateral safeguards agreement. Section 123 of the Atomic Energy Act requires that such agreements, once signed, be formally transmitted to Congress by the President together with a Nuclear Proliferation Assessment Statement (NPAS). This transmittal starts a fixed review period (roughly 90 days of continuous session); if Congress does not pass a joint resolution of disapproval, the agreement enters into force.

Following the July 22 signing, U.S. agencies stated the agreement "will now be transmitted to Congress for review," and Reuters reported the administration planned submission "within days." However, as of late July 2026, no source specified an exact date of formal transmittal. Earlier steps — an initial committee report in November 2025 and a February 19, 2026 notification of intent to negotiate an agreement omitting some traditional nonproliferation "guardrails" — concerned the intent to conclude the agreement rather than the final signed text.

Formal transmittal is typically documented via a Presidential message to Congress (published on the White House Presidential Actions page and printed in the Congressional Record) and a corresponding communication/referral record on Congress.gov. The distinction between an announced intent to submit and a documented formal transmittal is the central uncertainty for this question.

`{"format": "llm_question", "info": {"sdk_version": "0.5.0", "rating": {"quality": 3, "ambiguity": 3, "resolvability": 4, "passes": true}}}`
resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if, between July 22, 2026 and August 6, 2026 (inclusive), the President of the United States formally transmits the signed U.S.–Saudi Arabia civil nuclear cooperation ("Section 123") agreement to Congress under Section 123 of the Atomic Energy Act, triggering the statutory congressional review period. Formal transmittal is evidenced by a Presidential message to Congress transmitting the agreement, published on the White House "Presidential Actions" page (https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/), or by an entry recording the agreement's submission/referral to a congressional committee on Congress.gov, or by reporting from [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) that the signed agreement has been formally submitted to Congress. Statements of intent to submit "in the coming days" or general descriptions of the agreement being "pending congressional review" do NOT count; there must be a documented act of transmittal dated on or before August 6, 2026.
fine_print: The relevant act is the formal transmittal of the final signed agreement text (and accompanying documents such as the Nuclear Proliferation Assessment Statement) to Congress to begin the Section 123 review clock. Pre-signature notifications, such as the November 2025 committee report or the February 2026 notification of intent to negotiate, do not count. If the transmittal document is dated on or before August 6, 2026, the question resolves YES even if the record only becomes publicly viewable slightly after that date.

title: Will the UK–France-led multinational maritime mission begin escort or mine-clearance operations inside the Strait of Hormuz before August 7, 2026?
description:
Following the 2026 Iran crisis, which saw the Strait of Hormuz closed and mined during hostilities, the United Kingdom and France began organizing an "independent and strictly defensive" Multinational Military Mission to protect commercial shipping and clear an estimated ~80 naval mines from the strait. At a 17 April 2026 UK–France leaders' summit and a 12 May 2026 meeting where defence ministers and representatives from 38 nations issued a joint statement, the coalition committed to the mission, with a subsequent joint statement backed by 26 countries. Around a dozen militaries have prepared minehunters, naval vessels and surveillance assets; France and Britain agreed to shoulder most of the initial burden, with Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Denmark and Canada signaling potential contributions (some pending parliamentary approval). The UK forward-deployed the destroyer HMS Dragon and the minehunting mother-ship RFA Lyme Bay, while France staged frigates and minehunters.

Crucially, the coalition's joint statement specifies that "operations will only commence in a permissive environment" — that is, after a sustainable ceasefire and in accordance with international law and national constitutions. On 3 July 2026 the UK and France announced Oman had agreed to help keep its territorial waters safe, with initial efforts focused on the Gulf of Oman rather than the strait itself. At a 7 July 2026 NATO–Gulf ministerial meeting, France and Britain presented their plans, but Iran rejected the initiative; President Macron said the mission could start "within 2–3 days" if all parties concurred, but no concurrence emerged. Complicating matters, U.S. Central Command reinstated a naval blockade against Iran-linked vessels on 14 July 2026, straining the fragile mid-June interim accord. As of late July 2026, the mission was described as "ready and partially positioned" but with "operational deployment into the strait remains on hold," and no large-scale escort or mine-clearance inside the strait had been reported. Note that U.S. CENTCOM has conducted separate, unilateral mine-clearance operations in the strait, which are distinct from the UK–France-led multinational mission.

The Strait of Hormuz is the waterway connecting the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman between Iran and Oman/UAE. Operations conducted only in the Gulf of Oman, Arabian Sea, or Persian Gulf outside the strait itself do NOT count. Resolution will be based on reporting from [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions), including official statements from the UK Ministry of Defence, the French Ministry of the Armed Forces, or the mission coalition. If the coalition publicly declares that escort or mine-clearance operations have commenced inside the Strait of Hormuz, that suffices even if operational details are limited.

title: Will the Argentine Senate reach quorum to hold a plenary session on August 6, 2026?
description:
On July 16, 2026, the Argentine Senate opened a session with exactly the minimum quorum of 37 of its 72 members present, to debate the government-backed "ley de inviolabilidad de la propiedad privada" (which modifies the Ley de Tierras, easing land purchases by foreigners, and changes rules on expropriations and evictions). Lacking the votes to pass the bill, the ruling bloc (La Libertad Avanza, led in the Senate by Patricia Bullrich) moved to enter a "cuarto intermedio" (recess of an open session) until August 6, 2026; the motion passed 62–3 with 1 abstention. Earlier, on June 25, 2026, a scheduled session had fallen for lack of quorum when blocs declined to take their seats.

Quorum in the Senate is the absolute majority of the constitutional number of senators — 37 of 72 (Article 16 of the chamber's rules). Reaching quorum has repeatedly been contested, with opposition blocs at times deliberately denying it. When the session resumes on August 6, the government again depends on provincial and allied senators to seat at least 37 members and continue the debate. The Congress is in winter recess and is not expected to sit again until August.

The Senate publishes attendance within the Diario de Sesiones (stenographic version) for each session, listing present and absent senators, at senado.gob.ar.

It resolves NO if no plenary session reaches 37 senators present on August 6, 2026 (for example, if the session falls for lack of quorum or is postponed). Resolution is based on the official records of the Senate published at https://www.senado.gob.ar (the Diario de Sesiones / versión taquigráfica or official press releases for that date), or on [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) reporting on the session.

If the sitting is opened with 37+ present but later loses quorum, it still resolves YES. If the resumption is rescheduled to a later date before it reaches quorum on August 6, the question resolves NO.

title: Will Spain's agriculture ministry report bluetongue in at least 10 provinces for the 2026–2027 vector season by August 8, 2026?
description:
Bluetongue (lengua azul) is a viral disease of ruminants transmitted by Culicoides biting midges, notifiable in the EU. Transmission in Spain peaks in summer (July–August), when vector abundance is highest. Spain has 50 provinces. Each vector season, MAPA publishes "actualización de la situación epidemiológica" updates — roughly weekly during the 2025 vector season — and, for its per-province map, declares the first outbreak of each serotype in each province.

In the 2025–2026 season, bluetongue (serotypes BTV-1, BTV-3, BTV-8) spread widely; a UK government outbreak assessment citing Spanish data reported outbreaks in 25 Spanish provinces by 12 August 2025.

For the 2026–2027 vector season (first detections after the spring 2026 vector-free period), MAPA's update dated 22 July 2026 reported confirmed circulation in a small number of provinces — including A Coruña (BTV-8), Navarra (BTV-3), and Huesca (BTV-3), following earlier July detections in Galicia. As of late July 2026 the season tally stood at roughly 3–4 provinces.

Two forces pull in opposite directions. July–August is peak transmission and the virus is already widely seeded from the prior season, favoring rapid provincial spread. But in January 2026 the EU announced it would down-categorize bluetongue (from category C+D+E to D+E, effective July 2026), which may reduce the frequency and provincial detail of official reporting. MAPA's reporting cadence and provincial detail for 2026–2027 is therefore less certain than in 2025.

resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if the most recent "actualización de la situación epidemiológica" (epidemiological situation update) on bluetongue (lengua azul) published by Spain's Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food (MAPA) on its Bluetongue page (https://www.mapa.gob.es/es/ganaderia/temas/sanidad-animal-higiene-ganadera/sanidad-animal/enfermedades/lengua-azul/lengua_azul.aspx), and dated on or before August 8, 2026, indicates confirmed bluetongue virus circulation (any serotype) in at least 10 distinct Spanish provinces for the 2026–2027 vector season. The count is taken from MAPA's per-province tally/map for the 2026–2027 season shown in that update (MAPA declares the first outbreak of each serotype per province and builds a provincial map from these). This question is about the geographic spread of the disease as MAPA reports it: if the reported tally covers at least 10 provinces it resolves YES; if it covers fewer than 10 it resolves NO, regardless of whether the lower number reflects limited spread or less detailed reporting.
fine_print: Only outbreaks attributed to the 2026–2027 vector activity season (first detections after the winter vector-free period ending in spring 2026) count; provinces affected only in the 2025–2026 season do not count unless MAPA lists them as newly affected in 2026–2027. A "province" is one of Spain's 50 provinces (Ceuta and Melilla each count as at most one additional unit only if MAPA lists them separately). If the latest update no longer presents a per-province map or tally but MAPA's 2026–2027-season updates on the Bluetongue page collectively name the affected provinces in text, the resolver counts the distinct provinces named across those updates. If MAPA publishes no 2026–2027-season epidemiological update dated on or before August 8, 2026, the most recent available update on the Bluetongue page as of August 8, 2026 is used. If the MAPA Bluetongue page and its updates are permanently unavailable and the 2026–2027 province count cannot be determined from MAPA or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions), the question is annulled.

title: Will Andy Ogles win the 2026 Republican primary for Tennessee's 5th Congressional District?
description:
Tennessee's 5th Congressional District (TN-5) holds its Republican primary on August 6, 2026. Incumbent Rep. Andy Ogles, first elected in 2022 and re-elected in 2024, is seeking renomination. His main challenger is Charlie Hatcher, former Tennessee Commissioner of Agriculture (2019–2025), a livestock veterinarian and dairy farmer; Patrick Smith is also filed. In the 2024 GOP primary Ogles defeated challenger Courtney Johnston 56.5%–43.5%.

Ogles has been endorsed by former President Donald Trump and has received support from the Freedom Caucus Fund. Hatcher has been endorsed by former Gov. Bill Haslam, former Sen. Bob Corker, former Gov. Sonny Perdue, and former Rep. Zach Wamp, reflecting a split within Tennessee's Republican establishment. Hatcher has out-raised Ogles in direct campaign contributions: mid-2026 FEC reports showed Hatcher around $694,000 raised (including ~$133,000 self-funding) with ~$187,000 cash on hand, versus Ogles at ~$575,000 raised with ~$67,000 cash on hand and roughly $70,000 in debt. Outside groups have spent heavily on both sides. Ogles faces recurring campaign-finance controversies.

Tennessee's legislature redrew TN-5 ahead of 2026, extending the filing deadline to May 15. A Kalshi betting market cited by Axios showed Ogles' nomination odds falling from ~94% in May to ~64% by mid-July 2026. No independent public primary polls have been released.

title: Will an Ontario court grant a sale approval and vesting order for The Cannabist Company's asset sale to Vireo Growth before August 7, 2026?
description:

Completion is expressly conditioned on the Canadian Court granting a sale approval and vesting order under the CCAA, plus cannabis regulatory approvals in each state; the parties expect closings "in stages through calendar year 2026 and into 2027."

In CCAA sales, the debtor or Monitor brings a motion for an approval and vesting order before the Commercial List judge; the vesting order transfers the assets to the purchaser free and clear of prior claims. For reference, Cannabist's earlier Delaware and Ohio asset sales had purchase agreements dated March 23, 2026 and received court approval and vesting orders on April 15, 2026 — roughly three weeks after signing. In 2026 the tempo accelerated. The community "Russian Refinery Hitlist" recorded roughly 35 refinery strikes in the first five months of 2026. title: Will the SPC issue a Day 1 Moderate Risk (or higher) convective outlook on any day from July 1–9, 2026?
description:
The NOAA Storm Prediction Center (SPC) issues Day 1 Convective Outlooks several times daily (at roughly 0600, 1300, 1630, 2000, and 0100 UTC) categorizing the risk of severe thunderstorms across the contiguous United States. The categorical scale, from lowest to highest, is: Thunderstorms (TSTM), Marginal (MRGL, level 1/5), Slight (SLGT, level 2/5), Enhanced (ENH, level 3/5), Moderate (MDT, level 4/5), and High (HIGH, level 5/5). See https://www.spc.noaa.gov/misc/SPC_probotlk_info.html for category definitions.

A Moderate Risk (or higher) is issued on only about 14 days per year on average, concentrated in April–June. Climatological studies indicate the large majority of Moderate Risk days occur in spring, while July cases are comparatively uncommon and tend to be driven by damaging straight-line wind (derecho) events across the Plains, Midwest, and Ohio Valley. Many Julys see zero Moderate Risk days nationwide, though active summer patterns can produce them.

As of late June 2026, recent Day 1 outlooks topped out at Slight and Enhanced categories, with active low-pressure systems producing severe storms across the Great Plains, Ozarks, and Ohio Valley. SPC publishes all current and archived outlooks at https://www.spc.noaa.gov/products/outlook/ , and a date-searchable archive (since 2003) is available via https://www.spc.noaa.gov/archive/ .

Otherwise it resolves NO. The categorical outlook and its highest risk level can be checked for each day via the SPC Day 1 outlook page (https://www.spc.noaa.gov/products/outlook/) and the dated archive (https://www.spc.noaa.gov/archive/). A Moderate or High categorical area appearing in any one of the multiple daily issuances for any of these days is sufficient.
fine_print: "Day 1 Convective Outlook" refers specifically to the categorical convective (severe thunderstorm) outlook product, not the Day 2, Day 3, Day 4–8, fire weather, or thunderstorm outlook products. A day counts if any of that day's Day 1 issuances (including updates) contains a Moderate or High categorical risk area. The valid date is determined by the calendar date (UTC) of the outlook's valid period as labeled by SPC. Haredi rabbinic leaders have ordered their MKs both to push dissolution and to stop cooperating on the draft bill, leaving negotiations frozen and the final-reading timing uncertain. title: Will Turkey's Court of Cassation rule on CHP's appeal of the "absolute nullity" congress ruling before July 12, 2026?

Lawyers commenting in Turkish media (e.g., Ersan Şen) said that if the chamber decides the file without a hearing, a ruling could come before the recess; if a hearing is scheduled, a ruling would likely come after September 1. Several commentators (e.g., in Sözcü) noted a pre-recess ruling looks difficult given the time needed for the file to reach the chamber, a rapporteur report to be prepared, and the matter to be placed on the chamber's agenda.

title: Will any single 24-hour period between June 25 and June 28, 2026 see total crypto liquidations exceeding $1 billion, per CoinGlass?

title: Will Shakira's "Dai Dai" outpeak Shakira's "Waka Waka" on the Billboard Hot 100?
description:
The [2026 FIFA World Cup](https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026) will be co-hosted by the United States, Canada, and Mexico, with matches scheduled from June 11 to July 19, 2026. It will be the first World Cup to feature 48 teams and the first co-hosted by three nations.

On May 14, 2026, FIFA released ["Dai Dai"](https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/shakira-burna-boy-dai-dai-official-song) by Shakira and Burna Boy as the Official FIFA World Cup 2026 Song, in support of the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund. The song was unveiled at the Maracana Stadium and released globally across streaming platforms.

The benchmark for this question is Shakira's ["Waka Waka (This Time for Africa)"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waka_Waka_\(This_Time_for_Africa\)), the official song of the 2010 FIFA World Cup in South Africa. Waka Waka peaked at **#38 on the US** [Billboard Hot 100](https://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100/). It became the best-selling World Cup song of all time and one of the most-viewed music videos on YouTube, with multi-platinum certifications in numerous markets.

For comparison, here is how the official songs of the three most recent tournaments performed on the US Hot 100:

* **2014 Brazil** — ["We Are One (Ole Ola)"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Are_One_\(Ole_Ola\)) by Pitbull, Jennifer Lopez & Claudia Leitte peaked at **#11** on the Hot 100 (the only post-2010 World Cup song to outpeak Waka Waka).
* **2018 Russia** — ["Live It Up"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_It_Up_\(Nicky_Jam_song\)) by Nicky Jam, Will Smith & Era Istrefi did not chart on the Hot 100.
* **2022 Qatar** — ["Hayya Hayya (Better Together)"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayya_Hayya_\(Better_Together\)) and ["Tukoh Taka"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tukoh_Taka) neither charted on the Hot 100.
  Several factors may influence "Dai Dai"'s chart performance.

The tournament being co-hosted by the United States, the world's largest music market and the basis for the Billboard Hot 100, could increase the likelihood of a US chart hit. Shakira herself has an established US chart presence, and Burna Boy is one of the most globally successful Afrobeats artists, having previously charted on the Hot 100.

resolution_criteria:

fine_print:
Remixes, regional versions, and language variants of "Dai Dai" (or any other official song) will be treated as the same song for purposes of this question; the highest-charting version counts.

The Billboard Hot 100 (US version) is the chart of record. Other Billboard charts (e.g., Global 200, Hot Latin Songs) do not count for resolution.

title: Will Swiss voters approve the "No to a Switzerland with 10 million" population cap referendum?
description:
According to the [Federal Council](https://www.admin.ch/en/sustainability-initiative) (the official website of the Swiss government): 

> At the end of 2025, approximately 9.1 million people were living in Switzerland. Since the introduction of the free movement of persons in 2002, the population has grown by around 1.7 million. This is mainly due to immigration. The number of people immigrating depends primarily on the labour market. When the economy is strong, companies struggle to find enough workers within Switzerland. Companies, as well as public institutions like hospitals and care homes, often recruit the skilled workers they need from the EU.

> The ‘No to a Switzerland with 10 million! (Sustainability Initiative)’ calls for a cap on the permanent resident population: Switzerland’s population must remain below 10 million until 2050. If the permanent resident population exceeds 9.5 million before 2050, the Federal Council and Parliament will need to take measures, particularly in the areas of asylum and family reunification. The Federal Council would also need to invoke or negotiate exemptions and safeguard clauses in international agreements that contribute to population growth. If the 10-million threshold is exceeded, Switzerland would have to terminate these agreements, including the one with the EU on the free movement of persons after two years. This would also render the other agreements under Bilateral Agreements I null and void. Switzerland’s participation in the EU’s Schengen and Dublin agreements would also be called into question, thereby jeopardising close cooperation in the areas of security and asylum.

In order to pass, an initiative [requires](https://www.ch.ch/en/votes-and-elections/votes/popular-majority-and-majority-of-the-cantons/#when-is-a-popular-majority-and-a-majority-of-the-cantons-required) a "double majority" of both the popular majority nationally and the popular vote within a majority of Switzerland's cantons to vote yes.

title: Will a Ukrainian drone strike on the Russian port of Primorsk be publicly reported to cause damage between June 1, 2026 and June 14, 2026?
description:
The Russian Baltic Sea port of [Primorsk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primorsk,_Leningrad_Oblast) in Leningrad Oblast is Russia's largest oil-exporting port, operated by Transneft, and has become a recurrent target of Ukrainian long-range drone strikes during the Russo-Ukrainian War.

In 2026, several confirmed strikes have occurred:
- **March 23, 2026:** A Ukrainian long-range drone strike hit Transneft's fuel storage tanks at Primorsk, destroying or igniting at least four large tanks and forcing a shutdown of port operations. Leningrad Oblast Governor Alexander Drozdenko publicly confirmed the strike on his Telegram channel.
- **Mid-May 2026:** A wave of more than 60 drones targeted Primorsk and other Leningrad Oblast sites, hitting port infrastructure, a Karakurt-class missile corvette, a patrol boat, and shadow-fleet tankers. Drozdenko acknowledged the fire while saying no oil spill occurred; Zelenskyy claimed significant damage to port infrastructure.
- **Late May 2026:** Helsinki Times and Al Jazeera reported further strikes paralyzing Baltic oil exports from Primorsk, Ust-Luga, and Vyborg.

The Institute for the Study of War assessed at least 27 long-range Ukrainian strikes inside Russia since May 1, 2026, with rising tempo. No ceasefire is in effect, and both sides have escalated drone warfare through late May 2026.

`{"format": "llm_question", "info": {"rating": {"quality": 3, "ambiguity": 3, "resolvability": 4, "passes": true}}}`
resolution_criteria: This question resolves **YES** if, between 00:00 UTC on June 1, 2026 and 23:59 UTC on June 14, 2026, at least one Ukrainian drone (or other long-range unmanned aerial vehicle) strike on the port of Primorsk in Leningrad Oblast, Russia, is publicly reported to have caused damage — including but not limited to fires, damaged tanks/pipelines/buildings, damaged vessels at berth, or other physical damage to port or immediately adjacent infrastructure — as documented by [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/) or other [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). Confirmation by Leningrad Oblast Governor Alexander Drozdenko (e.g., on his Telegram channel) acknowledging damage from a drone strike at Primorsk also suffices. Resolves **NO** if no such strike causing damage at Primorsk is publicly reported within the window. Drone attempts that are reported as fully intercepted with no resulting damage do not count. Strikes on other Leningrad Oblast targets (Ust-Luga, Vyborg, St. Petersburg, etc.) do not count unless damage at Primorsk itself is reported.
fine_print: "Primorsk" refers to the port town and oil-export terminal in Vyborgsky District, Leningrad Oblast (not other Russian localities sharing the name). "Damage" means any physical damage reported by the named sources or by Russian officials, however minor; falling debris from an intercepted drone that ignites a fire or damages infrastructure at the port counts. If reporting is contested (Ukraine claims damage, Russia denies any), the question resolves YES only if at least one credible source affirms damage occurred. If a ceasefire halts all strikes for the full window with no reported attack on Primorsk, the question resolves NO.

title: Will a general Nintendo Direct be broadcast between June 1, 2026 and June 14, 2026?
description:
Nintendo Direct is Nintendo's series of online video presentations announcing upcoming games and hardware. "General" Directs are broad presentations covering Nintendo's overall lineup, typically 30-60 minutes long, distinguished from game-specific Directs (e.g., the May 6, 2026 "Star Fox Direct"), the "Nintendo Direct: Partner Showcase," "Indie World," "Pokémon Presents," and Mini presentations.

In recent years, Nintendo has typically held a summer general Direct in mid-to-late June around the time of Summer Game Fest (formerly E3): June 21, 2023; June 18, 2024; and June 18, 2025 (the 2025 June broadcast was the game-specific "Donkey Kong Bananza Direct"; the broader 2025 general Direct came September 12). For 2026, Nintendo has so far officially announced only the Star Fox Direct (May 6, 2026).

Reliable industry insider Jeff Grubb said on the Giant Bombcast in mid-May 2026 that he is "hearing there'll be a Nintendo Direct by mid-June," possibly around or after Summer Game Fest 2026 (which runs in early June). Other commentators (Nate the Hate) have echoed this. Nintendo typically announces Direct dates only a few days in advance via its official Twitter/X account and the Nintendo Direct landing page.

Historical base rates suggest that if a June Direct occurs, it most commonly lands in the third week of June (June 15-21), which is outside the resolution window. However, "by mid-June" rumors suggest it could occur earlier this year, and Summer Game Fest 2026 timing may pull the Direct into the first two weeks of June.

`{"format": "llm_question", "info": {"rating": {"quality": 3, "ambiguity": 3, "resolvability": 4, "passes": true}}}`
resolution_criteria:
This question resolves YES if Nintendo officially broadcasts a presentation branded as a "Nintendo Direct" (without a game-specific or sub-brand qualifier such as "Partner Showcase," "Indie World," "Pokémon Presents," "Mini," or a specific game title like "Star Fox Direct" or "Mario Kart World Direct") between 00:00 UTC on June 1, 2026 and 23:59 UTC on June 14, 2026. The broadcast must be a live or premiere video presentation made available on Nintendo's official YouTube channel and/or the Nintendo Direct landing page at https://www.nintendo.com/us/nintendo-direct/ during the window.

The primary resolution source is the Nintendo Direct archive/landing page at https://www.nintendo.com/us/nintendo-direct/ and the Wikipedia "Nintendo Direct" article's 2026 broadcast table at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_Direct. If a presentation titled simply "Nintendo Direct [date]" (or that Wikipedia classifies as a regular "Nintendo Direct" rather than a Partner Showcase, Indie World, Mini, or game-specific Direct) appears with a broadcast date in the window, the question resolves YES. Otherwise, it resolves NO.
fine_print:
- A "Nintendo Direct: Partner Showcase," "Indie World," "Pokémon Presents," "Nintendo Direct Mini," or any single-game-focused Direct (e.g., a hypothetical "Metroid Prime 4 Direct") does NOT count, even if Nintendo broadcasts one in the window.
- The relevant date is the original live broadcast/premiere date as published by Nintendo, regardless of regional time zone differences. If Nintendo's official posting lists the date as within June 1-14, 2026 (in any of Nintendo's official regional pages), the question resolves YES.
- If Nintendo announces during the window that a general Direct will occur after June 14, 2026, that does not count — only an actual broadcast in the window resolves YES.
- If https://www.nintendo.com/us/nintendo-direct/ is unavailable, the Wikipedia "Nintendo Direct" article or reporting from [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) will be used.

title: Will US spot Bitcoin ETFs record net inflows for the trading week ending Friday, June 12, 2026?
description:
US spot Bitcoin ETFs launched in January 2024 and have become a major channel for institutional and retail Bitcoin exposure. After strong inflows earlier in 2026, the complex entered a significant outflow phase in mid-to-late May 2026. Approximately $1.5 billion was pulled from US spot Bitcoin ETFs over roughly two weeks beginning around May 13, 2026, leaving year-to-date net inflows at approximately $536 million by the week of May 25, 2026. Major outflow days included May 13 (~$635M out), May 18 (~$649M out), and May 26 (~$334M out). BlackRock's IBIT and Fidelity's FBTC saw the largest redemptions, though IBIT remained net-positive for the year at roughly $2.7B.

Farside Investors publishes a daily-updated table of net flows (in US$ millions) across all US spot Bitcoin ETFs (IBIT, FBTC, BITB, ARKB, BTCO, EZBC, BRRR, HODL, BTCW, MSBT, GBTC, BTC) with a "Total" column summing all funds for each trading day. Whether the late-May outflow streak will continue into the week of June 8-12, 2026, or whether flows will reverse as dip-buyers step in, is genuinely uncertain.

`{"format": "llm_question", "info": {"rating": {"quality": 4, "ambiguity": 4, "resolvability": 4, "passes": true}}}`
resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if the sum of the daily "Total" net flow values across all US spot Bitcoin ETFs for the five trading days from Monday, June 8, 2026 through Friday, June 12, 2026 (inclusive) is greater than zero, as reported on the Farside Investors "Bitcoin ETF Flow - All Data" table at https://farside.co.uk/bitcoin-etf-flow-all-data/. The "Total" column on that page reports daily aggregate flows in US$ millions (e.g., a value of 120.5 means $120.5 million of net inflows). If Farside Investors is unavailable, the equivalent daily totals from SoSoValue's Spot Bitcoin ETF page (https://sosovalue.com/assets/etf/us-btc-spot) will be used as a fallback.
fine_print: If one or more of the five trading days (June 8-12, 2026) is an unscheduled US market closure, only the trading days that occurred will be summed. If Farside has not yet posted data for one or more of those days by end-of-day June 13, 2026 Eastern Time, the SoSoValue fallback will be used.

title: Will the Mark Twain Prize ceremony honoring Bill Maher remain scheduled at the Kennedy Center for June 28, 2026 as of June 14, 2026?
description:
On March 26, 2026, the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts officially announced that Bill Maher, longtime host of HBO's *Real Time with Bill Maher*, will be the 27th recipient of the [Mark Twain Prize for American Humor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Twain_Prize_for_American_Humor). The award ceremony is scheduled for June 28, 2026, at the Kennedy Center in Washington, D.C., with the show set to be recorded and later streamed on Netflix. The announcement came after some public confusion: an earlier report in *The Atlantic* about Maher receiving the prize was initially denied by White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt as "fake news," before the Kennedy Center confirmed via press release that Maher would indeed receive the honor.

The Kennedy Center has been operating performances at reduced capacity in 2025–2026. Past Mark Twain Prize honorees include Conan O'Brien (2025), Kevin Hart (2024), Adam Sandler (2023), and Jon Stewart (2022). The Mark Twain Prize is decided by an independent committee, not the Kennedy Center's board. The ceremony is one of the highest-profile programmed events on the Kennedy Center's 2025–26 calendar.

`{"format": "llm_question", "info": {"rating": {"quality": 3, "ambiguity": 3, "resolvability": 4, "passes": true}}}`
resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if, as of 23:59 ET on June 14, 2026, the Kennedy Center's official events calendar at https://www.kennedy-center.org/whats-on/calendar/ lists the Mark Twain Prize ceremony honoring Bill Maher as scheduled to take place on June 28, 2026 at the Kennedy Center. It resolves NO if, by that time, the event has been removed from the calendar, cancelled, postponed to a date other than June 28, 2026, or relocated to a venue outside the Kennedy Center complex, as indicated on the Kennedy Center website or reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). title: Will any Nvidia N1- or N1X-powered Windows PC be available for purchase by consumers before June 14, 2026?
description:
In late May 2026, Nvidia and Microsoft posted coordinated "a new era of PC" teasers pointing to Jensen Huang's Computex 2026 keynote in Taipei (May 31–June 1, 2026), with Microsoft's Build conference following on June 2. Industry coverage (Tom's Hardware, Windows Central, TechSpot, TweakTown) widely interprets the teaser as the formal debut of Nvidia's long-rumored ARM-based "N1" and "N1X" SoCs — co-designed with MediaTek and featuring a ~20-core ARM CPU paired with an RTX-class integrated GPU — running Windows on Arm.

The N1/N1X program was originally targeted for a Q3 2025 launch but was reportedly delayed into 2026 due to Windows on Arm software readiness, silicon revisions, and memory supply/notebook-demand headwinds. Leaks reference Dell, Lenovo, and possibly Alienware systems "being prepared for 2026," and a leaked motherboard image surfaced for an N1 laptop reportedly retailing around $1,400. However, no OEM has publicly committed to an on-sale date, and the typical gap between a Computex unveil and retail availability of a brand-new silicon platform is measured in months, not weeks.

This question asks whether any consumer can actually buy an N1- or N1X-powered Windows PC in the roughly two weeks between the expected Computex/Build announcements and June 14, 2026.

`{"format": "llm_question", "info": {"rating": {"quality": 4, "ambiguity": 4, "resolvability": 4, "passes": true}}}`
resolution_criteria:
This question resolves YES if, at any point between May 31, 2026 and 23:59 UTC on June 13, 2026, a Windows-based personal computer (laptop, desktop, mini-PC, or 2-in-1) whose primary system-on-chip is marketed by Nvidia and/or its OEM partners as the Nvidia "N1" or "N1X" (or a variant clearly using the same SoC family, e.g., "N1X Max") is offered for sale to ordinary consumers in at least one country, with the ability to place an order and receive shipment (or in-store pickup) of the device. Evidence can include a working "Buy" or "Add to Cart" button with stated availability/ship date on the website of a major OEM (e.g., Dell, Lenovo, HP, Asus, Acer, MSI, Microsoft, Alienware, Razer, Samsung) or a major retailer (e.g., Best Buy, Amazon, Newegg, JD.com), or a reputable news report from [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) confirming that such a device has gone on sale to consumers.

Pre-orders count as "available for purchase" ONLY if the OEM/retailer accepts payment or a binding order with a stated estimated ship date on or before July 31, 2026. Pure "register your interest," "notify me," or "coming soon" listings do NOT count. Developer kits, engineering samples, enterprise-only/B2B-only SKUs not offered to individual consumers, and the existing Nvidia DGX Spark / GB10-based mini-PC (which is a separate product line, not branded N1/N1X) also do NOT count.

If no such consumer-purchasable N1/N1X Windows PC is documented by 23:59 UTC on June 13, 2026, the question resolves NO.
fine_print:
If Nvidia and partners brand the chip with a different final retail name at launch (e.g., the SoC long rumored as "N1X" ships under a different marketing name), a device using that chip still counts as long as reputable reporting or Nvidia's own materials identify it as the same silicon previously referred to as N1 or N1X.

"Available to consumers" means an individual member of the public (not only enrolled enterprise customers) can complete a purchase transaction. Region-locked launches (e.g., China-only or US-only first wave) count. Listings that immediately sell out also count, provided actual orders were accepted.

title: Will Microsoft publish any official news about Project Helix on Xbox Wire between June 7 and June 14, 2026?
description:
Project Helix is Microsoft's codename for its next-generation Xbox console, first publicly introduced in a March 11, 2026 Xbox Wire post ("Building the Next Generation of Xbox") describing a custom AMD SoC-based system designed to play both Xbox console and PC games, with alpha developer kits planned for 2027. Microsoft has said additional information will come "later in 2026."

On the Official Xbox Podcast in late May 2026, Xbox CCO Matt Booty explicitly told viewers that the upcoming June 7, 2026 Xbox Games Showcase will NOT include Project Helix announcements, saying: "There won't be Helix news. Helix will not be in this Showcase." He indicated broader strategy and Helix topics will be saved for a later date.

Despite this denial, the showcase week is the highest-attention window of the Xbox calendar, and Microsoft sometimes shares hardware-adjacent updates via Xbox Wire blog posts around major events. The question asks whether any official post explicitly mentioning Project Helix appears on Xbox Wire (news.xbox.com) during that week.

title: Will Apple explicitly mention or display "Google" or "Gemini" during the WWDC 2026 keynote on June 8, 2026?
description:
Apple's Worldwide Developers Conference (WWDC) 2026 keynote is scheduled for Monday, June 8, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. Pacific Time, livestreamed from Apple Park and available on apple.com, the Apple Developer app, the Apple TV app, and Apple's YouTube channel. The keynote is the marquee opening presentation where Apple announces its new operating systems and major platform features for the coming year.

On January 12, 2026, Apple and Google issued a joint statement announcing a multi-year collaboration in which the next generation of Apple Foundation Models will be based on Google's Gemini models and Google Cloud infrastructure, powering future Apple Intelligence features including "a more personalized Siri coming this year." Multiple reports (Mark Gurman/Bloomberg, AppleInsider, TechCrunch) since have indicated that the Gemini-backed Siri overhaul is expected to debut at WWDC 2026 as part of iOS 27.

Despite the public joint statement, Apple is reportedly reluctant to highlight Google's role on stage because Google is widely associated with advertising, which clashes with Apple's privacy branding. Historically, Apple does mention partner AI vendors on stage when integrating them — for example, at WWDC 2024 and WWDC 2025 Apple repeatedly mentioned "ChatGPT" by name during the keynote. However, in WWDC 2025 Apple did not mention "Google" in the spoken keynote narration, even though Google was referenced as a searchable service in the accompanying press release.

title: Will the June 2026 University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment number be greater than it was for May 2026?
description:
NPR Michigan Public May 27, 2026 by Edith Pendell: [Consumer confidence reaches all-time low amid rising gas prices, UM study finds](https://www.michiganpublic.org/economy/2026-05-27/consumer-confidence-reaches-all-time-low-amid-rising-gas-prices-um-study-finds)

> The U of M [<u>Surveys of Consumers</u>](https://www.sca.isr.umich.edu/)' May 2026 index of consumer sentiment dipped to a record low in its third consecutive month of decline. Consumer sentiment measures how optimistic or pessimistic people feel about their personal finances and the broader economy. According to Director Joanne Hsu, nearly 40% of people interviewed for the May survey mentioned gas prices when asked about their personal finances. The U.S. military campaign in Iran has caused [<u>supply disruptions</u>](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/27/business/hormuz-global-shortages-gas.html) in the Strait of Hormuz. The Strait is vital for oil and natural gas shipping. Hsu said people primarily experience geopolitical situations like the conflict in the Middle East through their impacts on the prices of everyday items. The surveys, collected monthly, also measure people’s feelings about their personal financial prospects and how they expect factors like unemployment, interest rates, and inflation to change in the future. The group has been collecting data across the United States since 1946.

A FRED chart with the complete data can be found [here](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/UMCSENT).

title: Which U.S. Supreme Court Justices will vote in favor of Monsanto in Monsanto Company v. John L. Durnell? (Samuel A. Alito, Jr.)
description:
On April 4, 2025, Monsanto Company, a subsidiary of Bayer AG, filed a petition for a writ of certiorari with the U.S. Supreme Court in the case [Monsanto Company v. John L. Durnell](https://law.justia.com/cases/missouri/court-of-appeals/2025/ed112410.html). The case arises from a Missouri state court decision where a jury [awarded](https://blog.cvn.com/1.25m-verdict-in-zero-offer-case-breaks-monsantos-roundup-trial-winning-streak) \$1.25 million in damages to John L. Durnell, who alleged that exposure to Monsanto's glyphosate-based herbicide, Roundup, caused his non-Hodgkin's lymphoma.

Monsanto's [petition](https://content.presspage.com/uploads/2809/4203e574-9a0c-49ee-9476-8ba63ba6e424/4.4.2025monsantov.durnellcertpetition.pdf?10000) argued that the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA) preempts state-law failure-to-warn claims, especially since the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has approved Roundup's labeling without a cancer warning. The petition highlighted a split among federal appellate courts on this preemption issue, noting that while the Third Circuit has held that FIFRA preempts such state-law claims, the Ninth and Eleventh Circuits have reached the opposite conclusion.

On January 16, 2026, the Supreme Court [agreed to hear the case](https://www.supremecourt.gov/docket/docketfiles/html/public/24-1068.html). The Court will decide whether federal pesticide law prevents plaintiffs from bringing state-law claims that Roundup should have included a cancer warning, given that EPA did not require such a warning.

Merits briefing has since been completed. The United States filed an [amicus brief supporting Monsanto](https://www.justice.gov/d9/2026-03/24-1068_monsanto_tsac.pdf), arguing that FIFRA preempts Durnell’s failure-to-warn claim, and the Court granted the Solicitor General’s request to participate in oral argument. The case was argued on April 27, 2026, with Paul Clement arguing for Monsanto, Sarah Harris for the United States, and Ashley Keller for Durnell. As of May 28, 2026, the Court has not issued a decision.

resolution_criteria:

If the Court does not issue a merits decision before August 1, 2026, all subquestions will be **annulled**.
fine_print:
Justices who concur only in the judgment will resolve as **Yes**, as long as they vote to reverse, vacate, or otherwise set aside the Missouri state court judgment against Monsanto.

If the Court affirms the judgment of the Missouri court, Justices who dissent will resolve as **Yes** as long as they indicate that they would have reversed, vacated, or otherwise set aside the Missouri court’s judgment.

title: Will Minnesota’s prediction-market ban be blocked by a federal court order on August 1, 2026?
description:
On May 18, 2026, Minnesota approved SF 4760, an omnibus public-safety bill that includes Article 8, a new prediction-market ban. The law defines “prediction market” broadly and makes it a felony to create, operate, manage, control, facilitate, advertise, or market covered prediction-market activity. The prediction-market section is effective August 1, 2026, and applies to crimes committed on or after that date.

On May 19, 2026, the CFTC filed a federal lawsuit against Minnesota seeking to block the law, saying it would criminalize activity in CFTC-regulated event-contract markets and interfere with federal regulation of derivatives markets. The CFTC said it is seeking a preliminary injunction to stop the law from going into effect on August 1, 2026.

This dispute comes as prediction markets expand into new areas. Reuters reported that Polymarket launched markets tied to private-company performance through an agreement with Nasdaq Private Market, with Nasdaq Private Market serving as a resolution data provider for those private-company markets.

title: Will Japan's retrial reform bill (amendment to the Code of Criminal Procedure) pass the House of Representatives before May 31, 2026?

title: Will the Joint Commission (Comissão Mista) on Brazil's MP 1.357/2026 approve its report (parecer) before May 31, 2026?
description:
On May 12, 2026, Brazil's federal government published Medida Provisória (MP) 1.357/2026 in the Diário Oficial da União, amending Decree-Law 1.804/1980 and authorizing the Ministry of Finance to zero the 20% federal import tax on international purchases up to US$50 — the so-called 'taxa das blusinhas' affecting purchases from platforms like Shein, AliExpress, and Shopee. The MP took effect immediately, with the zero rate implemented via a Finance Ministry portaria scheduled to take full effect around May 27, 2026.

Under Brazil's Constitution and Joint Resolution 1/2002 of Congress, every Medida Provisória must be analyzed first by a bicameral Joint Commission (Comissão Mista) composed of deputies and senators. This commission elects a president and a rapporteur (relator), receives amendments, and approves a written opinion (parecer) recommending approval of the MP as-is, approval with changes (via a Projeto de Lei de Conversão), or rejection. Without the Joint Commission's approved parecer, the MP cannot normally proceed to plenary votes in the Câmara dos Deputados and Senado Federal — although in practice, when commission opinions are delayed, plenaries sometimes vote on the basis of a relator's opinion delivered orally on the floor.

As of May 17, 2026, on the official Congresso Nacional tramitation page (https://www.congressonacional.leg.br/materias/medidas-provisorias/-/mpv/174123): the amendment window runs through May 18, 21 amendments have been filed, and the Joint Commission was designated on May 15, 2026 but its full membership list was scheduled to be published in the Diário do Congresso Nacional on May 21, 2026. No relator has yet been named, and no parecer has been issued. The urgency regime — which locks the agenda of whichever chamber holds the MP — begins June 26, 2026, and the initial 60-day deadline is July 10, 2026. Historically, many Brazilian MPs do not see a Joint Commission parecer approved until well into the second half of the 120-day window, but politically salient and government-priority MPs sometimes move much faster.

`{"format": "llm_question", "info": {"rating": {"quality": 3, "ambiguity": 3, "resolvability": 4, "passes": true}}}`
resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if, before May 31, 2026 (Brasília time), the Joint Commission (Comissão Mista) designated to analyze Medida Provisória 1.357/2026 has formally approved a parecer (opinion/report) on the MP, as reflected on the official tramitation page at https://www.congressonacional.leg.br/materias/medidas-provisorias/-/mpv/174123 (for example, the page records 'Parecer aprovado pela Comissão Mista' or an equivalent registered approval of a commission opinion). A commission parecer that recommends rejection still counts as a YES, as the parecer itself was approved. Mere designation of a relator, presentation of a draft parecer that has not been voted on, or plenary votes that bypass the commission do NOT count. Otherwise the question resolves NO.
fine_print: If the official Congresso Nacional tramitation page is unavailable, the resolver may use the Câmara dos Deputados or Senado Federal official tramitation pages for MPV 1357/2026, or reporting from [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). If MP 1.357/2026 is withdrawn, rejected by either plenary, or otherwise terminated before a Joint Commission parecer is approved, the question resolves NO.

title: Will the SPC issue at least one High Risk Day 1 Convective Outlook between May 17 and May 30, 2026?
description:
The NOAA/NWS [Storm Prediction Center (SPC)](https://www.spc.noaa.gov/) issues Day 1 Convective Outlooks several times daily, assigning a categorical risk level for severe thunderstorms across the contiguous United States. The five categorical levels, from lowest to highest, are: Marginal (1/5), Slight (2/5), Enhanced (3/5), Moderate (4/5), and High (5/5). A "High Risk" indicates the most dangerous severe weather setup — typically a major tornado outbreak or widespread destructive wind event — and is issued only a few times per year on average (roughly 3 per year, with substantial year-to-year variation, and clustering in April–May).

Beginning with the 1630Z Day 1 outlook on March 3, 2026, the SPC introduced a Conditional Intensity Group (CIG) overlay on hazard-specific probability maps, but the five categorical risk levels (Marginal, Slight, Enhanced, Moderate, High) and their names and meanings were retained.

As of May 17, 2026, no High Risk Day 1 outlook has been issued in 2026; the most recent documented High Risk on record was April 2, 2025 (the Arkansas/Mid-South tornado outbreak). The current SPC Day 1 outlook (issued 17/0100Z) is at Enhanced Risk. Late May is climatologically near the peak of the U.S. severe weather season.

If the SPC issues a High Risk Day 1 outlook on May 16, 2026 (before the window) or after May 30, 2026, that does not count.

title: Will a new publicly reported cybersecurity incident affecting Antel, HG S.A., Tickantel, or TuID Digital be reported between May 18, 2026 and May 28, 2026?

- **Tickantel (reported May 15, 2026):** The threat actor "DeadPresidents" published ~1 GB of data from Tickantel's development servers (including FTL templates and hardcoded credentials), reportedly obtained via lateral movement from a prior compromise of HG S.A. Local threat-intel firm BCA LTD characterized this as a direct consequence of the HG breach.

Several Latin-America-focused leak actors (LaPampaLeaks, DeadPresidents, BogotaLeaks, Uruguayo1337) appear actively engaged against Uruguayan state-linked systems, and remediation of the underlying credential exposure is ongoing.
